2024.EP9.11.t: Update on Hosting FIFA World Cup 2026
2024.EP9.11.s:
In 2018, the 2026 World Cup was awarded to a joint bid by Canada, United States, and Mexico. The World Cup is the largest single sporting event held in the world and rivals the Summer Olympics as the largest overall. It is held every four years over six weeks. In 2026, the World Cup will be expanded to include 48 countries and 104 matches from the current 36 countries, playing 64 games. There will be 6 matches held at Exhibition Place - BMO Field.

The event is the world's most-watched sporting event, with a global viewership of four billion people for the entire competition and upwards of 200 million for each match. Overseen by the International Federation of Football Association (FIFA), the World Cup generates significant economic and cultural benefits for host cities. On June 16, 2022, the City of Toronto was announced as an official Host City.

As directed by City Council in 2022, the FIFA World Cup Toronto 2026 Staff Secretariat was established to support project planning, preparation, and execution of the event.

The Executive Director and Project Manager from the City Secretariat Office will attend the Board meeting on April 25, 2024, to present an update on the planning and progress to the Board Members.

2024.EP9.15.t: Safe, Affordable, Reliable, Innovative, Transit (SARIT) Micro Mobility Electric Vehicle Pilot Program
2024.EP9.15.s:
This report provides information on the collaboration of Exhibition Place with SARIT (Safe, Affordable, Reliable, Innovative, Transit) Micro Mobility Electric Vehicle Pilot Program which is an initiative by York University.

Exhibition Place signed a no cost one-year agreement Memorandum of Understanding with York University to allow for the testing and to provide feedback on the SARIT Micro Mobility Electric Vehicle.

Exhibition Place will serve as a testbed for the SARIT Prototype, a three-wheeled micro mobility battery operated vehicle boasting a 100-kilometer range https://saritmobility.com/. The Pilot Program will test 4 SARIT electric vehicles.

The partnership with York University aims to demonstrate how the integration of micro-mobility electric vehicles can contribute towards achieving the city's greenhouse gas reduction targets, which set at 45 percent reduction by 2025, 65 percent reduction by 2030, and net zero by 2040 from 1990 levels. This collaboration aligns with the shared vision of both Exhibition Place and York University to diminish environmental impact and operational costs associated with fleet vehicles.

2024.EP9.19.s:
The purpose of this report is to provide a status update on the potential wastewater energy project at Exhibition Place and recommend next steps.

Sewer wastewater contains recoverable heat with the ability to displace natural gas use in buildings and therefore significantly reduce Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions, consistent with TransformTO goals.

City Council provided staff with direction to engage with Noventa Energy Partners (Noventa) on up to 9 additional projects following the work on the initial project at Dundas and Bathurst with UHN Toronto Western Hospital. Noventa is engaging potential customers/partners (multi-building campuses) around the City on these project opportunities, as they have financing from the Canadian Infrastructure Bank (CIB) to support their projects.

Exhibition Place was identified as a potential opportunity given the need to replace existing aging equipment in the coming years, and City direction on working toward net-zero emissions. Exhibition Place represents an opportunity to showcase city action on net-zero at a priority location and demonstrate Toronto's leadership in the renewable energy field and as a technological innovation hub.
